=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text data "7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0"
text tidx "indices: "
global vals long 8
global idx ulong 3
global sub3 long 3
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note show writes vals[0..n-1] separated by spaces, then a newline
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
emiti get vals i
end
emit nl
end
note sorts the three indices, gathers their values, sorts those, and writes them back in index order;
note both sorts are three compare-exchanges, enough for three elements
fn cx3u to void
for p ulong 3
i = rem p 2
if gt get idx i get idx add i 1
t = get idx i
put idx i get idx add i 1
put idx add i 1 t
end
end
end
fn cx3l to void
for p ulong 3
i = rem p 2
if gt get sub3 i get sub3 add i 1
t = get sub3 i
put sub3 i get sub3 add i 1
put sub3 add i 1 t
end
end
end
fn main to int
n = parse data
put idx 0 6
put idx 1 1
put idx 2 7
show n
emit tidx
emitu get idx 0
emit sp
emitu get idx 1
emit sp
emitu get idx 2
emit nl
cx3u
for i ulong 3
put sub3 i get vals get idx i
end
cx3l
for i ulong 3
put vals get idx i get sub3 i
end
show n
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
indices: 6 1 7
7 0 5 4 3 2 1 6
</pre>
